rounds.response:
We should accept modest compromises (five‑month fact period, rolling productions, up to six depositions per side) to demonstrate reasonableness and conserve resources, but hold the line against any blanket stay of expert discovery and against pre‑committing to an early summary‑judgment schedule that would limit our ability to take necessary depositions or bring targeted early motions after core production.  
Proposed discovery plan language for the Rule 26(f) report: Fact discovery: five months from service of initial disclosures; Document production: rolling productions beginning 30 days after initial disclosures with substantial completion of core liability documents (project schedules, change orders, communications, payment records, agreed custodial ESI) within 90 days; Depositions: up to six fact depositions per side, taken after substantial completion of core productions unless otherwise agreed; Expert discovery: no blanket stay—exchange expert identifications within 30 days after substantial completion of core productions, opening reports due 60 days thereafter and rebuttal reports 30 days later; ESI/privilege protocol: parties to meet and confer and submit an agreed protocol and rolling privilege log.  
Talking points for the 26(f) call on expert timing: we are not seeking to proliferate expert work but cannot accept a blanket stay because expert analysis is often necessary to test technical defenses and is more efficient if timed predictably after core documents are produced; our proposed 30/60/30 timetable gives both sides clarity and avoids serial delays.  
Talking points on the early‑motion schedule: we propose not to hard‑wire Opposing Counsel’s contemplated partial SJ schedule because whether an early motion is appropriate and what scope it should have depends on what emerges in document production and initial depositions; if a party intends to seek early summary judgment it should notify the other side and meet and confer on timing and scope before seeking a Court‑set schedule.  
We can present this as a cooperative, proportional plan in the joint report while expressly reserving all rights to seek tailored relief if the record warrants.
